_source: Primary structure: UNDRR-ISC Hazard Information Profiles (HIPs) 2025 — 7 of 8 hazard clusters (Extraterrestrial omitted as out of scope for urban climate adaptation). Hazards within clusters draw from C40/Arup Climate Hazard Typology (city-level climate hazards) and Resilient Cities Catalysts (RCC) taxonomy (non-climate acute shocks and slow-onset stresses).
_note: Restructured in v0.1.1 from C40/Arup-primary to HIPs 2025-primary. Each cluster carries c40_arup_categories[] for legacy crosswalk. Each hazard carries c40_arup_category (the legacy C40/Arup parent), hazard_source ('c40_arup' or 'rcc'), and undrr_terms[] for matching UNDRR-framed source documents. The previous rcc_non_climate and rcc_slow_onset buckets were dissolved — their contents now sit in their proper HIPs clusters (Technological, Societal, Geohazards, Environmental). v1.2: every hazard has a one-line definition stating its boundary with its nearest neighbour; water_stress and coastal_erosion added; rcc.sea_level_rise now means sea level rise only; overlapping undrr_terms de-duplicated (Decision 53).

hazards.name: Coastal flood
hazards.definition: Flooding of coastal land by the sea: high tides, king tides or storm-driven water above normal levels. Use storm_surge for the surge itself and rcc.sea_level_rise for the slow rise in mean sea level.

hazards.name: Flash/surface flood
hazards.definition: Flooding from intense rainfall that overwhelms drainage or soil before reaching a river (pluvial, surface-water or urban flooding), including flash floods in small, steep catchments. Use river_flood when a river overtops its banks.

hazards.name: Groundwater flood
hazards.definition: Flooding caused by the water table rising above the ground surface or into basements and underground structures.

hazards.name: River flood
hazards.definition: Flooding when a river, stream or lake overtops its banks or defences (fluvial flooding). Use flash_surface_flood for rainfall flooding away from watercourses.

hazards.name: Cyclone (Hurricane/Typhoon)
hazards.definition: A tropical cyclone of hurricane or typhoon strength (sustained winds of about 119 km/h or more), with its wind, rain and surge treated as one event. Use tropical_storm for weaker systems.

hazards.name: Severe wind
hazards.definition: Damaging wind not from a tropical cyclone or tornado: windstorms, extratropical storms, derechos, downbursts, and dust or sand storms.

hazards.name: Tornado
hazards.definition: A rotating column of air in contact with the ground, typically from a thunderstorm.

hazards.name: Tropical storm
hazards.definition: A tropical cyclone below hurricane or typhoon strength (tropical depression or tropical storm).

hazards.name: Heavy snow
hazards.definition: Heavy snowfall, snowstorms and blizzards that disrupt movement, load structures or isolate places.

hazards.name: Rain storm
hazards.definition: Intense or prolonged rainfall as a weather event. Use flash_surface_flood or river_flood when the text describes the resulting flooding.

hazards.name: Extreme hot weather
hazards.definition: Hot conditions as a seasonal or long-term regime: hotter summers, more hot days and nights, rising average temperatures. Use heat_wave for a discrete multi-day event.

hazards.name: Heat wave
hazards.definition: A discrete event of several consecutive days with temperatures above a local threshold. Use extreme_hot_weather for hotter seasons or a warmer climate in general.

hazards.name: Cold wave
hazards.definition: A discrete event of several consecutive days with temperatures below a local threshold. Use extreme_cold_weather for cold seasons or frost in general.

hazards.name: Extreme cold weather
hazards.definition: Cold conditions as a seasonal or recurring regime: severe winters, hard freezes and frost. Use cold_wave for a discrete multi-day event.

hazards.name: Ice, hail, freezing rain
hazards.definition: Ice storms, freezing rain, glaze, sleet and hail.

hazards.name: Fog
hazards.definition: Fog dense enough to disrupt transport or operations.

hazards.name: Electrical storm
hazards.definition: Thunderstorms and lightning as a hazard to people, structures or power and communication systems.

hazards.name: Storm surge
hazards.definition: A temporary rise of sea level driven by a storm's winds and low pressure. Use coastal_flood for tidal flooding without a storm, and cyclone_hurricane_typhoon when the whole cyclone is the subject.

hazards.name: Drought
hazards._note: HIPs 2025 groups drought under water-related Meteorological & Hydrological hazards.
hazards.definition: A prolonged period of below-normal precipitation that leaves too little water for ecosystems, agriculture or supply (meteorological, agricultural or hydrological drought). Use water_stress when demand persistently outstrips supply, with or without a dry spell.

hazards.name: Water stress
hazards.definition: A chronic gap between water demand and available supply, from overuse, growth or a declining resource, whether or not there is a drought. Use drought for a temporary shortfall in precipitation.

categories.name: Geohazards
categories._note: Geophysically-triggered hazards. Includes tsunami (HIPs 2025 places tsunami in Geohazards because its trigger is geophysical, not meteorological). Includes both acute shocks (earthquake, volcanic) and chronic/slow-onset processes (subsidence).

hazards.name: Avalanche
hazards.definition: A rapid flow of snow or ice down a slope.

hazards.name: Landslide
hazards.definition: The movement of rock, earth or debris down a slope, including debris flows and mudslides. Use rockfall for falling rock and rcc.liquefaction for earthquake-driven ground failure.

hazards.name: Rockfall
hazards.definition: Rock falling, bouncing or sliding from a steep slope or cliff.

hazards.name: Subsidence
hazards.definition: A sudden or localised sinking of the ground, such as a sinkhole or collapse. Use rcc.subsidence_chronic for gradual, widespread sinking over years.

hazards.name: Coastal erosion
hazards._note: v1.2 (Decision 53): split from rcc.sea_level_rise ('Sea Level Rise / Coastal Erosion'), which named two hazards. The id has no rcc. prefix; hazard_source carries the source.
hazards.definition: The loss of land, beaches, dunes or cliffs at the coast to waves, currents and storms, including shoreline retreat. Use rcc.sea_level_rise for the rise in sea level itself.

hazards.name: Tsunami
hazards._note: Reclassified from wave_action to geohazards in v0.1.1 to align with HIPs 2025, which groups tsunamis under Geohazards based on geophysical trigger.
hazards.definition: A series of sea waves caused by the displacement of water, usually by an earthquake or landslide.

hazards.name: Earthquake
hazards.definition: Ground shaking from a sudden release of energy in the earth's crust.

hazards.name: Volcanic Activity
hazards.definition: Eruptions and their effects: lava, ash fall, gases and pyroclastic flows.

hazards.name: Liquefaction
hazards._note: Seismic-induced ground failure. Distinct from C40 mass_movement subsidence: liquefaction implies earthquake trigger.
hazards.definition: Ground losing strength and behaving like a liquid during earthquake shaking.

hazards.name: Subsidence (chronic / non-seismic)
hazards._note: Distinct from C40 mass_movement subsidence: refers to long-term ground settling from groundwater extraction, soil compaction, or peat oxidation rather than acute geophysical events.
hazards.definition: Gradual, widespread sinking of the land over years, from groundwater extraction, soil compaction or peat loss. Use subsidence for a sudden, local collapse.

categories.name: Environmental
categories._note: Slow-onset environmental degradation and wildfire. HIPs 2025 places wildfire under Environmental hazards alongside biodiversity loss, air quality, and sea level rise.

hazards.name: Forest fire
hazards.definition: Uncontrolled fire in forest or woodland, including bushfires and wildfire at the urban edge.

hazards.name: Land fire
hazards.definition: Uncontrolled fire in grassland, savanna or scrub.

hazards.name: Sea level rise
hazards.definition: The long-term rise in mean sea level and its chronic effects: permanent inundation of low land and higher baselines for tides and surges. Use coastal_erosion for loss of shoreline material and coastal_flood for flooding events.

hazards.name: Environmental Degradation
hazards.definition: The decline of soil, land, water or ecosystem quality from human pressure, such as contamination or degraded land. Use rcc.loss_of_biodiversity when species or habitat loss is the subject.

hazards.name: Loss of Biodiversity
hazards.definition: The loss of species, habitats or ecosystems.

hazards.name: Poor Air Quality (chronic)
hazards.definition: Persistent or recurring air pollution (particulate matter, ozone, smog) at levels harmful to health.

hazards.name: Invasive Species
hazards.definition: Non-native species that spread and harm ecosystems, agriculture or infrastructure.

hazards.name: Air-borne disease
hazards.definition: Disease spread through the air between people or from the environment, such as influenza or respiratory epidemics. Use rcc.disease_outbreak when the text names an outbreak without its mode of transmission.

hazards.name: Insect infestation
hazards.definition: Outbreaks of insects or other pests that damage crops, forests, buildings or stored goods.

hazards.name: Vector-borne disease
hazards.definition: Disease carried by mosquitoes, ticks or other vectors, such as dengue, malaria or Lyme disease.

hazards.name: Water-borne disease
hazards.definition: Disease spread through contaminated water, such as cholera.

hazards.name: Disease Outbreak
hazards._note: General outbreak framing. Use when a source describes a disease event without specifying transmission mode (use the more specific air-borne / vector-borne / water-borne entries when transmission is documented).
hazards.definition: An outbreak, epidemic or pandemic when the text does not state how it spreads. Use air-borne_disease, vector-borne_disease or water-borne_disease when it does.

hazards.name: Ocean acidification
hazards.definition: The fall in seawater pH from absorbed carbon dioxide, harming marine life and fisheries.

hazards.name: Salt water intrusion
hazards.definition: Seawater moving into freshwater aquifers, rivers or soils.

hazards.name: Hazardous Materials Accident
hazards.definition: An accidental release of hazardous chemicals or materials, such as an industrial spill.

categories.name: Technological
categories._note: Promoted to first-class cluster in v0.1.1 (previously buried under rcc_non_climate). Critical for modeling cascading climate-induced infrastructure failures (e.g., heatwave → grid failure → health impacts).

hazards.name: Cyber Attack
hazards.definition: A deliberate attack on, or failure of, digital and communication systems that disrupts city services.

hazards.name: Power Outage
hazards.definition: A loss of electricity supply over an area, whatever its cause. Use rcc.infrastructure_failure for failures of other systems.

hazards.name: Infrastructure Failure
hazards.definition: The failure of critical infrastructure other than the power supply, such as a dam, bridge or water main, including cascading failures.

hazards.name: Nuclear Incident
hazards.definition: An accident or release at a nuclear facility.

categories.name: Societal
categories._note: Promoted to first-class cluster in v0.1.1 (previously buried under rcc_non_climate). Important for modeling indirect impacts of climate migration, displacement, and resource conflict.

hazards.name: Riot / Civil Unrest
hazards.definition: Riots, civil disorder and sustained social unrest.

hazards.name: Terrorist Attack
hazards.definition: Deliberate violence intended to cause fear or harm to further political or ideological aims.

hazards.name: Financial / Economic Crisis
hazards.definition: A financial crisis, recession or economic shock that hits city revenues, jobs or households.
